annotations.title: Run a Monte Carlo simulation of a model

description: Runs a Monte Carlo simulation of a model and returns the full range of possible outcomes, not one guessed number. A model is a set of uncertain inputs, the formulas that combine them, and the links between them. The simulation draws random values for every input many times; each draw is a trial, and one call is one run. Use this when you need to know how likely different outcomes are for a plan built on uncertain inputs: a project's total cost or budget (for example from low / most likely / high estimates per line item), a schedule or delivery date, capacity, revenue, or an investment's NPV, IRR or payback. It returns a summary: for each output node (the nodes nothing else depends on, or the ones you list in run_params.output_request.nodes) the mean, the 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles (the value that share of trials fall below), the minimum and maximum in the last time period, and the same per period; plus any metrics you asked for, such as NPV, IRR, payback or the chance of beating a target or budget; and a run_id. Pass that run_id to get_simulation_results for other nodes, periods or percentiles. A run that takes longer than about 40 seconds keeps running in the background: you get status running and a run_id, and get_simulation_results gives you progress and then the result. Cost: without an account, 1 of your 3 free runs per UTC day, for a model up to 1,000 trials and 20 nodes; that daily allowance is counted per network address and client, so on a shared platform such as Claude.ai or ChatGPT you may find today's free runs already spent by someone else. Signed in with a free Kromatic account, 1 of 10 free runs per UTC day, for a small model up to 10,000 trials and 50 nodes, spent before any credits. Beyond that -- a larger model, or a day whose free runs are used up -- 1 credit for a small run or 5 for a large one, currently $0.50 per credit; buy_credits tops up. A model that is invalid, or over the limits of the tier you are in, is rejected before running and costs nothing. If it fails mid-run, it depends on the tier: without an account the free run is still used up and not given back; signed in on a free run, the free run is given back; on credits, you are not charged. That last rule is this tool's own: rank_inputs_by_impact is different, because it charges credits when its analysis starts and keeps them if it fails.

AggregationRequest.description: A financial metric computed over one node's whole time series in every trial, then summarized as a distribution. Available: npv (net present value), irr (internal rate of return), mirr (modified IRR), payback and discounted_payback (periods until cumulative cash turns positive), cagr (compound annual growth rate), cumsum (running total), terminal_value, and prob (the chance a value passes a threshold). Discounting counts periods from 0: the first period is not discounted. Model an up-front investment as a negative value in period 0. Do not also discount inside the node's formula with PV() or DISCOUNT(), which count from 1, or the first period is discounted twice. cumsum gives one number per trial: the total of the node's values over every simulated period. output_request.time_periods does not shorten it. prob can target any earlier metric, including npv and cumsum. Its mean in the result is the probability, the share of trials that pass. A prob that targets a node directly only tests the node's final-period value. Recipe for the chance that a cumulative total over the first N periods beats X: add {id: total, function: cumsum, target_node_id: <node>}, then {id: p, function: prob, target_aggregation_id: total, params: {op: '>', value: X}}, and read aggregations.p.basic_stats.mean. This works directly when the model has exactly N periods. If it has more, point cumsum at a calc node with formula IF({time_period} <= N, {e1}, 0). {time_period} counts from 1. Use cumsum and prob for totals and probabilities here. A running-total node is needed only for rank_inputs_by_impact and summarize_outcome_scenarios, which measure one node in one period.

function.description: One of npv, irr, mirr, payback, discounted_payback, cagr, cumsum, terminal_value, prob. npv needs rate, a decimal per period (0.01 is 1%), so a model with monthly periods needs a monthly rate (10% a year is about 0.008 a month); or rates, a list of per-period decimals with at least one entry per period; the first entry is ignored because period 0 is not discounted. discounted_payback needs rate. terminal_value needs g (growth) and rate. mirr needs finance_rate and reinvest_rate. prob needs op (>, >=, <, <=, ==) and value.

CalcNode.description: A formula node. Its formula combines the values on its incoming edges. There is no automatic sum: write {e1}+{e2} to add two edges, or {e1} to pass one through. A node with no formula is always 0, and check_simulation_model reports that as a warning.

formula.description: Expression over incoming edge ids in braces, for example '{e1} * 0.5 + {e2}'. Leave it out only if the node should always be 0. Operators: + - * / ^ (power) and parentheses; dividing by zero gives 0. Comparisons == != < <= > >= work inside IF. Functions (any case): MIN, MAX, ROUND, ABS, POW, SQRT, LOG, LN, EXP, FLOOR, CEIL, SUM, PRODUCT, AVERAGE, MEAN, IF(condition, then, else), AND, OR, NOT, PV(rate, value, period), DISCOUNT(rate, period), BINOMIAL, INDEX(edge, k) for the k-th item (from 1) of a list value, LENGTH. Special values: {time_period} is the current period counted from 1 (unlike the 0-based time_period arguments), {is_first} and {is_last} are 1 on the first or last period and 0 otherwise.
formula.title: Formula

delay.description: How many periods to wait before the first draw. Default 0.

distribution_params.description: The distribution's parameters. Which keys are needed depends on distribution_type: normal{mean,std}, log_normal{mu,sigma}, uniform{low,high}, triangle{min_val,max_val,mode_val}, beta{alpha,beta}, poisson{lambda_val}, bernoulli{p}. Other types are listed in this schema's oneOf.
distribution_params.title: Distribution Params

distribution_type.description: The distribution's name. Which to pick: beta for a rate or proportion (its values lie between 0 and 1, so 2% is 0.02); log_normal for a positive amount that can run high; normal for a symmetric quantity; uniform or triangle when you know hard limits; gamma or exponential for waiting times; poisson, binomial, discrete_normal, discrete_lognormal or discrete_gamma for whole-number counts; bernoulli for yes or no (1 or 0); categorical for a fixed list of possible values; constant for a known value. dirichlet, multivariate_normal and constant_array produce a list of values per trial; read one item with INDEX({edge}, k). Each type's parameters are in this schema's oneOf.
distribution_type.title: Distribution Type

id.description: Unique id for this node within the model.
id.title: Id

interval.description: Draw a new value every N periods; in the periods between, this input is 0 (the value is not carried forward). 1 (the default) means every period. 0 means draw once, in the first period after any delay, and 0 afterwards. To keep one value in every period, use sampling_frequency once instead.
interval.title: Interval

sampling_frequency.description: per_period (the default) draws a new value each period. once draws one value per trial and reuses it in every period.
sampling_frequency.title: Sampling Frequency

RootNode.title: RootNode

output_request.description: Optional. Limits what the result includes and adds financial metrics such as NPV.

time_periods.description: How many time periods to simulate in each trial (a count, not an index). A period is whatever unit you choose: month, quarter or year.
time_periods.title: Time Periods

trials.description: How many trials to run. A trial is one random sample of every input and the outcomes that follow from it. More trials give smoother results.
trials.title: Trials

detail.description: How much to return. summary (the default): the output nodes' mean, 10th/50th/90th percentiles, minimum and maximum, a compact per-period series, and your metrics. full: every node and edge in every period with histograms, cut down with a truncation note if it would be too large for the client. Prefer summary, then ask get_simulation_results for the specific numbers you need.
detail.title: Detail

graph.description: The model. A model has four parts. root_nodes are the uncertain inputs; each one draws a value from a probability distribution in every trial. calc_nodes are formulas that combine values. edges are links that carry a value from one node to another; a formula refers to its incoming edges by id, like {e1} * {e2}. run_params sets how many trials (random samples) and time periods to simulate. A time period is whatever unit the model's author chooses, such as a month, quarter or year. run_params.time_periods is a count, while time_period arguments and output_request.time_periods are indices counted from 0: with 12 monthly periods, index 11 is month 12. Formula syntax is described on calc_nodes[].formula. Common distributions and their parameters: normal{mean,std}, log_normal{mu,sigma}, uniform{low,high}, triangle{min_val,max_val,mode_val}, beta{alpha,beta}, poisson{lambda_val}, bernoulli{p}.

seed.description: Optional whole number that fixes the random draws, so repeating the call gives the same result. Exact repeats are guaranteed only for small runs, where trials × nodes × time periods is at most 100,000.
seed.title: Seed
